label: def:chern-character
title: The Chern character of a quantum universe
html:
Definition. The Chern character of a quantum universe

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over R, with Grothendieck group K_0(\mathbf{C}) and degree-zero Hochschild homology HH_0(\mathbf{C}), the direct sum of the endomorphism modules of the objects modulo the relations fg = gf.

Definition. The Chern character of \mathbf{C} is the homomorphism

  \mathrm{ch} \colon K_0(\mathbf{C}) \longrightarrow HH_0(\mathbf{C}), \qquad [X] \longmapsto [\mathrm{id}_X],

sending the class of an object to the Hochschild class of its identity morphism. It is well defined because \mathrm{id}_{X \oplus Y} = \mathrm{id}_X \oplus \mathrm{id}_Y and the two summands are orthogonal, so [\mathrm{id}_{X \oplus Y}] = [\mathrm{id}_X] + [\mathrm{id}_Y] [bghl-2017].

The block presentation. By Wedderburn semisimplicity the central idempotents p_\lambda \in \operatorname{End}(A), one per block \lambda \in \widehat{A}, span HH_0(\mathbf{C}): every endomorphism of a simple object is a scalar, every object is a sum of simple ones, and morphisms between different blocks contribute nothing to the cocenter. So HH_0(\mathbf{C}) \cong R^{\widehat{A}}, spanned by the classes [p_\lambda] = [\mathrm{id}_{V_\lambda}], and in this basis

  \mathrm{ch}\Bigl(\sum_\lambda n_\lambda [V_\lambda]\Bigr) \;=\; \sum_\lambda n_\lambda\, [p_\lambda] \;=\; (n_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}} .

The Chern character is therefore the map \mathbb{Z}^{\widehat{A}} \to R^{\widehat{A}} induced by the ring map \mathbb{Z} \to R: injective when R has characteristic zero, and in every case an isomorphism after tensoring with R.

The factorisation of the quantum dimension. The rigid trace \mathrm{tr} \colon \operatorname{End}(X) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R of a rigid monoidal category satisfies \mathrm{tr}(fg) = \mathrm{tr}(gf), so it descends to a linear map

  \mathrm{ev} \colon HH_0(\mathbf{C}) \longrightarrow R, \qquad \mathrm{ev}[p_\lambda] = \dim_q(V_\lambda),

and the quantum dimension on K_0(\mathbf{C}) is the composite

  K_0(\mathbf{C}) \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{ch}\ } HH_0(\mathbf{C}) \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{ev}\ } R, \qquad \dim_q = \mathrm{ev} \circ \mathrm{ch}.

This is the statement proved in the Lean carrier (dimQK0_eq_evDimQ_chernCharacter). Its content is a separation of roles: the Chern character records which simple constituents an object has and how many times, an integer datum independent of q; the evaluation records what the trace assigns to each block, which is where q enters. A quantum dimension is one number obtained from the whole character by one evaluation — for the group \mathrm{SU}(2), the evaluation at the pivotal element of a Laurent polynomial whose evaluation at 1 is the ordinary dimension, as the next example makes explicit. It is not itself an Euler characteristic of anything, and the base curve's Euler characteristic, which is an alternating sum over all the Hochschild degrees of a different object, is not obtained from it.
